subject: Temporary view-only access + MFA note for SOC 2 evidence review
messages:
From: Sally Thompson <sally.thompson@acmehealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Health Audit Team <audit@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: access window extension for SOC2 evidence review

Diego —

Our external auditor started the evidence review this morning and ran into an issue with the trust portal invite you sent last week. The SSO flow keeps returning a 401 (we use Okta, and the auditor's account is outside Acme's org). They were able to see the initial index page but not download the encrypted bundles required for the control walkthrough.

Can Redwood:
- Extend the portal access window by 48 hours (we need until end of day Friday Pacific)
- Provide a view-only, non-SAML fallback option or a one-time download link for the auditor so they can retrieve the evidence without forcing Okta again

We also need a bridge letter that confirms the report covers the audit period through June 30, 2026 and notes any residual exceptions. If you can attach the bridge letter (PDF) that would help our compliance log.

All the best,
Sally Thompson
Senior Compliance Manager
Acme Health Systems

--
Acme Health Audit Team
audit@acmehealth.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Thompson <sally.thompson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: access window extension for SOC2 evidence review

Thanks for the heads up, Sally — and sorry for the friction.

Quick answers:
- I've extended the existing portal invite for Acme auditors to expire 2026-09-19T23:59:00-07:00 (48 extra hours).*
- We generally prefer SSO for audit access, but we can issue a one-time, view-only fallback link that bypasses the customer's IdP for downloads if the auditor cannot complete SSO.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly (cc'd) will generate a one-time view-only download link and attach the bridge letter PDF.
2) If the auditor needs full bundle downloads, the fallback link will allow that for a single session and then expire. Otherwise, we can share a zipped evidence bundle via an encrypted S3 link and rotate the key immediately after download.

Notes about scope: The bridge letter will explicitly reference the SOC 2 Type II period ending 2026-06-30 and call out that there were no material exceptions beyond the ones documented in the report.

Apologies again for the SSO issue — we'll follow up with engineering to see why Okta-based external accounts are inconsistent through the portal.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Trust & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_bridge_letter_202609.pdf (will be attached by Kimberly)

*Portal expiration updated in audit log: https://trust.redwood.ai/portal/audit-log/entry/EX-20260917-xx
From: Acme Health Audit Team <audit@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Sally Thompson <sally.thompson@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: access window extension for SOC2 evidence review

Diego / Kimberly —

We tried the expanded window but are still hitting the same 401 on SSO when we attempt to download the encrypted evidence bundles. The auditor reported: "Okta redirect completes, we land on /portal/acme-2026-soc2, then a 401 on /api/evidence/download?bundle_id=..."

A one-time fallback link would be ideal. Could you also include any short instructions for using the link (incognito browser, clearance checkbox, IP allowlist note) so our auditors don't get blocked again?

Thanks — we aim to complete downloads by Friday.
- Audit Team
